# Tom Lee Issues Rare Bearish Ethereum Warning

Top Ethereum ETHUSD bull and co-founder of Fundstrat Tom Lee has issued a very unusual bearish alert for the second-largest crypto.

According to his latest post on X, Lee sounded an alarm about the potential negative impact of the dramatic stock market drop in South Korea on the crypto market, which may trigger more ETH sell-offs. [...] "This major decline in Korean equities is likely spilling over into crypto," Lee wrote. Lee expressed serious concern about South Korean brokerages' margin liquidations. He also mentioned the fact that South Korean investors hold a large share of crypto, and the crypto asset market is vulnerable to financial contagion. "Short-term pain," he continued, and highlighted ETH. [...] Lee issued the bearish alert at a time when South Korea's benchmark KOSPI dropped over 6% on Tuesday, Oct. 13 due to the massive sell-off in technology and semiconductor stocks. The stock market crash was so severe that the Korea Exchange had to take emergency market stabilization measures.

What's happening in South Korea?

According to Tom Lee, chairman of Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH) treasury company Bitmine Immersion Technologies (NYSE: BMNR), this sell-off has huge potential implications for crypto. Most notably, it could lead to a sell-off in Ethereum, the one digital asset that his company has been hoarding since June 2025. [...] That's where crypto enters the picture. South Korea is a hotbed of crypto activity, and many tech investors there are also crypto investors. Thus, some investors could be forced to sell off their crypto holdings, partly as a way to make up for the losses now being incurred on their tech stock holdings.

Person in office at night, staring at trading screens.

Image source: Getty Images. [...] On the surface, there might not be a clear connection between Ethereum and what's happening in South Korea and other Asian markets. Here's the thing: The overseas tech sell-off has already resulted in forced liquidations. In turn, says Lee, this activity could lead to a wave of "secondary" liquidations.
